findings.issue: PR_SET_DUMPABLE silently accepts but retains no security state; GET hardcoded zero. Ordinary same-UID own child remains readable and its FD duplicable after successful SET0.

Proc auxv/environ/fd readlink have no alien access gate; proc template always assigns target effective owner regardless of dumpability. A common AlienAccess fix alone does not close all confirmed paths.
Capability LSM returns immediately on matching IDs, omitting Linux commoncap caller-effective/permitted versus target-permitted superset check. Not runtime tested here.

minimal_fix_direction: Model dumpability as memory-image state (ProcessVm/Vmar), share with CLONE_VM/threads, inherit on fork, initialize ordinary successful exec to USER. Core-dump generation itself is not required for access isolation.
PR_GET returns retained state; PR_SET accepts only0/1 and changes real state. Failed exec and failed/no-op/query credential calls must preserve the appropriate old state.

Ordinary cross-process access must read credentials then dumpability coherently and require USER unless target-user-namespace CAP_SYS_PTRACE permits it, followed by all existing LSM/Yama/trusted-image guards. Same-thread-group introspection remains separately permitted.

Credential effective/fs UID/GID changes and relevant capability gains must reset dumpability before publishing changed credentials; inspect Linux commit_creds ordering and exec credential/VMAR activation. Existing credential atomics are relaxed and are not an established publication interlock.

Do not recursively acquire process.lock_vmar in check_alien_access: current maps/mem callers already hold it. Use an explicit locked snapshot/helper or a rigorously ordered credential/image guard; define lock ordering for new pidfd checks and avoid holding VMAR through waits for target ptrace stops.

Add original READ_FSCREDS access to auxv/environ/fd paths and Linux-compatible dynamic proc owner behavior. For auxv/environ use per-open VM image snapshot like existing maps/mem and Linux proc_mem_open, so already-open descriptors cannot follow a privileged new image. This latter lifecycle risk is source-only here.

Do not blindly apply the new ordinary attach dumpability gate to PTRACE_TRACEME: this kernel routes only voluntary TRACEME through do_ptrace_attach, while PTRACE_ATTACH is unimplemented. Linux has a distinct voluntary tracing hook.

Retain limits/namespace/user identity and existing G1 image guards. Test different-UID/capability exceptions, shared-VM/fork and failed/successful privilege exec in subsequent isolated phases; do not claim all same-UID interactions isolated.
